question: Does a modest, continuation-only tune raise actual late-wave contact and overlap pressure for funded large fleets without changing the early game or forcing an optimizer loss?

method.setup: Idealized finite candidate poses. Every drone is bought through ordinary tryAnchor using earned scrap and per-type prices. No bonus resources, recalls, repositions or combat pose edits.
method.pairing: Generate each baseline paid placement plan once, then freeze exact poses, types and purchase waves for both candidate replays. Assert identical prices, legal affordable purchases and unchanged recorded campaign score. No adaptive candidate fleet re-optimization.
method.pilot: Idle in waves1–7 and9–11; ordinary bounded steering/pitch/thrust pursuit in8 and12 from one legal idealized staging position. Perfect state knowledge and immediate reactions; no human skill claim.
method.policies: Pierce and mixed references retain the previous growth-trial policies. Diversified policy keeps eight opening Pierce, then buys the cheapest next type with a maximum four Stasis; this is an earned larger fleet example, not a reconstruction of the unknown human32-drone layout.
method.measures: Actual HP reductions and terminal states are observed synchronously before pool reuse. Drone damage attribution is independently reconciled with contribution totals. Hull-seconds integrate remaining living HP over time. Route fractions and enemy-seconds include actual world-space slow behavior. Hit-contact seconds count frames with actual HP loss times dt, including terminal hits; they describe activity across all weapons, not continuous Pin projectiles or nominal route coverage.
method.pinBreakpoint: Wisps remain at1.1 hull (47.52HP) in all continuation waves, below two24-damage Pin shots. Raising them to1.15 or1.2 would require three isolated Pin shots, a disproportionate50% shot-count increase; Shards retain the modest later progression.
method.limitations: One seed and three deliberately strong finite-search policies. Not optimal play, win rates, browser rendering, larger-fleet performance, human difficulty or evidence that every fleet should leak. More hull may increase useful contact without adding breaches.
